page: Microsoft Azure L80s_v4 is a storage-optimized server belonging to the Lsv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 80 virtual CPUs mapped to 40 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The system is equipped with 640.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 8.0 GB per core, and includes 19,199 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the L80s_v4 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, achieving a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 21,672.0 and a strong stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 69,325.3. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the average tier. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 5,387.5 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 223.47 GB/sec for large-block reads. The server also excels in data processing tasks, registering top-tier performance in static web serving throughput at 105.75 GB/sec and image processing. Database operations are robust, with Redis SET operations reaching 91.92 million operations per second.

The qualitative cost profile of the L80s_v4 reflects its high resource density, combining massive local NVMe storage with a high-capacity memory array. This configuration offers a balanced tradeoff for data-intensive workloads that require high-speed local scratch space without the latency of network-attached storage. The presence of AMX instructions enables efficient local LLM inference, with prompt processing for a 7B model reaching 275.51 tokens per second. This server is suited for large-scale relational and non-relational databases, high-throughput web serving, data warehousing, and localized machine learning inference tasks.
